title: Japan's Egg Prices at Record Highs
paragraphs: Eggs are an important part of many meals in Japan. But they are now more expensive than ever before.

According to Japan's agriculture ministry, a pack of 10 eggs cost an average of 312 yen in October. This is the highest price since the ministry began its monthly survey in August 2003. The price was 3 yen higher than in September.
For the survey, the ministry checked prices at 10 stores in each of Japan's 47 prefectures between October 19 and 21. It announced the results on October 27.
Egg prices have been high for most of this year. In June, the average price was 309 yen, the same as the previous high in March and May. Now the price has gone up again.

There are several reasons why eggs are so expensive. First, many people buy more eggs at the end of the year, so demand is growing. Second, Japan is still feeling the effects of last year's bird flu outbreak. When bird flu is found at a farm, all the chickens there usually have to be killed to stop the disease from spreading. This means fewer chickens are laying eggs.
In addition, the cost of chicken feed has gone up. Japan imports much of its feed, and the weak yen makes imported products more expensive.
Eggs are not the only food with high prices. The prices of chicken and imported beef also matched their previous records in October.
Higher food prices are putting pressure on many families in Japan. Since eggs are used in so many dishes, people may feel the change in their daily lives.
